subject: Commercial bridge request — Telemetry SDK delay impacting onboarding
messages:
From: Alice Tran <alice@acmeinc.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeinc.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry SDK delay — onboarding impact and commercial ask

Hi Ava / Karthik,

Quick note from my side — our onboarding team hit a hard blocker this week. The telemetry SDK that we were told would be available in the March SDK bundle is still missing key hooks (session-level traces + event batching) which we rely on for our usage dashboards. Without it we can’t complete the POC rollout to our pilot users, and that pushes our GA timeline by ~6 weeks.

Our procurement team is asking if Redwood can provide a short-term commercial bridge while the SDK work finishes. Specifically: a temporary credit to offset our expected overage during the delayed ramp and a small rate discount for the first two months after GA.

We’re happy to be transparent about usage and timelines — attached is a short note from our engineering lead outlining the missing telemetry pieces and the impact (acme_onboarding_gap_notes.pdf).

Can we get a plain answer from Redwood on whether this is feasible and what approval path looks like? We’d prefer not to pause onboarding.

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Inc

---

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tran <alice@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry SDK delay — onboarding impact and commercial ask

Thanks for the clear note and attachment, Alice — really helpful. Sorry you’re blocked.

Internal note for Karthik / Marissa / Ben: Acme is asking for a temporary commercial bridge + short-term discount while our telemetry SDK gaps are closed. They’re asking for both (credit for overages during delayed ramp + a discounted rate for first 2 months post-GA).

Proposed internal ask: provisional credit equal to 30% of projected incremental usage for the next 8 weeks (we have the forecast from Acme in the attachment), and a 20% usage-rate discount for the first 60 days after they’re back on a normal ramp. This would be timeboxed, non-recurring beyond the window, and implemented as a billing adjustment (not a change to list pricing).

Immediate next steps I need from you all to move this to execs:
- Karthik: confirm ETA for SDK fixes and a high-level risk statement (can we commit to a ship date within 3 weeks?).
- Marissa: confirm commercial precedent and whether the proposed structure (credit + 60d discount) is acceptable to Sales Ops.
- Ben: confirm finance gate (what level of approval is required for a credit of this magnitude) and whether we can make the adjustment in the billing system quickly if approved.

Alice — we’ll loop back quickly. If it helps, we can propose a documented ‘bridging letter’ that spells the exact terms for procurement to approve.

— Ava
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry SDK delay — onboarding impact and commercial ask

Short update from product: we’ve triaged the missing hooks — session traces and event batching are in active sprint. Engineering believes we can deliver a v1 of the hooks within 18 business days (target ship: 2028-03-26) assuming no further priority changes. Risk: if a critical bug appears in the new batching path it could slip another 1–2 weeks.

I’ve attached a quick comp calc I ran to show the sensitivity (comp_bridge_calc.xlsx). Recommendation to Sales/Finance: approve a timeboxed bridge (either a % credit or a $ cap) to keep pilot momentum. Given the ETA I’d be comfortable with a 2-month discount window rather than 3.

If we need to elevate, I can summarize impacts for the exec ask (product timeline, customer risk, remediation plan) — recommend we propose a provisional credit of up to $40k (or 30% of incremental usage, whichever is lower) plus a 20% discount for the first 60 days after GA.

— Karthik
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry SDK delay — onboarding impact and commercial ask

Thanks for the context and the quick product timeline. Ben — for finance: per policy we need exec approval for any commercial credit above $25k. Acme’s ask falls into that bucket if we go with Karthik’s $40k ceiling.

Operational decision (provisional, pending exec sign-off): we can offer a billing adjustment structured as follows to present to Acme procurement:
- Provisional credit: up to $30k (applied as a one-time credit on next invoice) — this is our preferred upper bound for a quick approval.
- Post-GA discount: 20% usage rate discount for first 60 days after SDK ship.
- Must be timeboxed in writing; credit applied only if the SDK delivery slips beyond the committed date.

Action items:
- Ava: present this package to Acme (I drafted language below you can use).
- Ben: please confirm the approval path & estimated time to make the billing adjustment if execs sign off. If exec review required, route to VP Sales and CFO for authorization.
- Karthik: lock the target ship date in a short note that we can include in the bridging letter.

Draft bridging language for procurement: "Redwood agrees to provide Acme Inc a one-time credit of up to $30,000 should the Redwood Telemetry SDK not meet the mutually agreed ship date of 2028-03-26. Additionally, Redwood will apply a 20% usage-rate discount for 60 days following GA to assist Acme during ramp. This package is time-limited and applies only to the Acme pilot referenced in Deal ACME-2028-3-02."

Once Ben confirms the approval path I will take a quick exec note to get sign-off.

— Marissa
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

---
